overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the three allegations (individual notice, unlisted topic, outside deliberation) and declined to review a fourth that was not an OML issue.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board had to give him written notice because it discussed him at its February 14 meeting, which he was not told about.
allegations.key_passage: However, an individual has a right to individualized notice only when the individual is the subject of an executive session convened under Purpose 1.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board discussed his conduct at its February 14 meeting, a topic not listed on the notice posted 48 hours before.
allegations.key_passage: We have not been presented with evidence that the Board's chair anticipated discussion of Ms. Bolduc's complaint 48 hours before the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Feb. 27 chair statement differed from the Feb. 14 vote, indicating deliberation by the Board outside a noticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the town administrator did not facilitate communication between or among a quorum of the public body, the changes to the statement did not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board requested an investigation into the purpose of a resident's actions and who authorized them.
allegations.key_passage: Because this allegation, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, we decline to review it.
